Rashi on Shabbat 102a:10:1.english: In the mouth of the furnace - And it was burned in the flame.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:10:2.hebrew: הכא דקא מיכוין - מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום, דהא אחשביה:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:10:2.english: Here, where he intended [to throw it there] - His intention renders it a [valid] place [of rest], since he attached significance to it.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:11:2.hebrew: ד' חטאות - משום חלב, משום נותר, משום אכילת יוה"כ, משום טומאת הגוף ואכל קדש:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:11:2.english: Four sin-offerings - Because of forbidden fat, because of notar, because of eating [on] Yom Kippur, [and] because of bodily impurity [when] he ate consecrated [food].

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:11:3.hebrew: ואשם מעילות - דאפילו הוא כהן, גבי אימורים זר הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:11:3.english: And a guilt-offering for misuse [of consecrated items] - For even [if] he is a priest, regarding sacrificial portions he is [considered] a non-priest.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:12:1.hebrew: אף אם היתה שבת כו' - ומשום יוה"כ לא מיחייב בהוצאה, דקסבר אין עירוב והוצאה ליוה"כ:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:12:1.english: Even if it was Shabbat, etc. - And because of Yom Kippur he is not liable for carrying out, because he holds [that the laws of] eruv and carrying out do not apply to Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:12:2.english: It is not of the [same] category - This sin-offering is not due to eating, but rather due to carrying out.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:12:3.hebrew: ואמאי - מיחייב משום הוצאה לדברי הכל? הא אין דרך להוציא בפה:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:12:3.english: And why - is he liable for carrying out according to everyone? Behold, it is not the [usual] way to carry out [an object] in [one's] mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:12:4.hebrew: מחשבתו - שצריך לאוכלה בהליכתו, ואחשבה להוצאה זו בפיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:12:4.english: His thought - For he needs to eat it while walking, and he deemed this carrying out in his mouth [significant].

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:1:2.english: And he remembered - that it is Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:1:3.english: After [it] left - the stone from his hand, and before it comes to rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:1:4.hebrew: קלטה אחר - קס"ד לאחר שנזכר זה קלטה אחר; הוו להו שנים שעשאוה, וכגון שנעקר ממקומו וקבל. או שקלטה כלב בפיו, דלא הויא הנחה, דבעינן מקום ד' — פטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:1:4.english: Another caught it - We initially thought [the Mishnah means] that after this [thrower] remembered, another caught it; [in that case] they are two who performed [the labor], such as where [the catcher] moved from his place and caught [it]. Or where a dog caught it in its mouth, which is not [a valid] placing down, since we require a place of four [handbreadths] — [therefore he is] exempt.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:2:1.hebrew: ופרכינן הא נחה - לסוף ד' ברה"ר, חייב, ואע"ג דנזכר בין עקירה להנחה. והא קתני סיפא זה הכלל כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:2:1.english: And we ask: [If] it came to rest - at the end of four [cubits] in the public domain, [he is] liable, even though he remembered between the lifting and the placing. Yet does not the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teach: "This is the general rule," etc.?

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:2:2.english: The latter clause - Which teaches: "unless their beginning and their end are unwitting."

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:2:3.hebrew: אתאן ללכתא ומיתנא - לכתא — עץ קטן שכפול ראשו, וצריך לחמורים נושאים דרדורים של יין, שתוחבין אותו בשני עקלים שהדרדורים תלויין בהן משני צידי החמור, ומחברים בו הדרדורים שיחזיק זה את זה:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:2:3.english: We have come to [a case of] a lakhta and a cord - A lakhta [is] a small piece of wood whose tip is bent over, and it is needed for donkeys carrying barrels of wine; for they insert it into two loops from which the barrels hang on both sides of the donkey, and they connect the barrels with it so that one holds the other [in place].

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:2:4.hebrew: ומתנא - חבל. כלומר, לא מיתוקמא סיפא אלא בזורק לכתא הקשור בחבל קטן כדרכו, ואוחז החבל בידו, וכשנזכר היה בידו לאחוז החבל ולעכב זריקת הלכתא שלא תנוח; הלכך, תחילתו שוגג וסופו מזיד, ופטור. אבל זרק צרור וחפץ, שכשנזכר אין בידו לעכבו, כוליה שוגג הוא; ונזכר דקתני ברישא אשמעינן רבותא, דאף על גב דנזכר לא מיפטר מחטאת אא"כ קלטה אחר או כלב:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:2:4.english: And a cord - A rope. That is to say, the latter clause [of the Mishnah] is only established [as referring] to one who throws a bolt tied to a small rope in its usual manner, while holding the rope in his hand, so that when he remembered, it was in his power to grasp the rope and restrain the throw of the bolt so that it would not come to rest; therefore, its beginning [was] unwitting and its end [was] intentional, and he is exempt. However, [if] he threw a pebble or an object, where once he remembered it is not in his power to restrain it, the entire [act] is unwitting; and [the case of] "he remembered" that is taught in the first clause teaches us a novel point: that even though he remembered, he is not exempt from a sin-offering unless another [person] or a dog caught it.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:1.hebrew: ופרכינן לכתא ומתנא אוגדו בידו - ואפילו כוליה מילתא שוגג, לא מיחייב, דאין כאן זריקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:1.english: And we ask: "The bolt and the cord — one holds it in his hand" - And even [if] the entire matter [was done] unwittingly, he is not liable, for there is no throwing here.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:2.hebrew: כגון שנתכוין לעשות חבורה - בתחלתו בשגגת שבת, ונזכר עד שלא נעשית החבורה. ולעולם בלכתא ומיתנא, וכגון שנתכוין לעשות חבורה כו', דהאי משום זכירה הוא דמיפטר, שהיה בידו להחזיר, נמצא סופו זדון. הא לא נזכר, חייב, ואע"ג דאגדו בידו, דחיוביה לאו משום זריקה הוא אלא משום חבורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:2.english: Where one intended to inflict a wound - [i.e.,] at its beginning [he acted] in unwitting violation of Shabbat, and he remembered before the wound was inflicted. And still [we are dealing] with a bolt and a cord, and [the case is] where he intended to inflict a wound, etc., for this one is exempt on account of remembering, since it was in his power to pull [it] back, [so] it turns out its end [was] intentional. However, [if] he did not remember, he is liable, even though he holds it in his hand, because his liability is not on account of throwing, rather on account of [inflicting] a wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:3.hebrew: הא בהדיא קתני לה - במתניתין, ו"זה הכלל" ע"כ למילתא אחריתי אתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:3.english: This was taught explicitly - in the Mishnah, and [the clause] "this is the general rule" necessarily comes [to teach] another matter.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:4.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - זה הכלל, למעביר ארבע אמות ברה"ר ונזכר קודם שהעבירו ד' אמות אתא, שהיה בידו לעמוד במקום שנזכר, אבל זורק לא מיפטר בזכירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:3:4.english: Rather, Rava said - [The Mishnah's phrase] "this is the general rule" refers to one who carries [an object] four cubits in the public domain and remembers before he has carried it four cubits, since it was in his power to stop at the place where he remembered; whereas one who throws is not exempted by remembering.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:4:1.hebrew: והא כי קתני זה הכלל אזריקה תני לה - דאיירי לעיל מיניה בזורק לעשות חבורה, ואי סתם זורק לא מיפטר בזכירה, היכי מתני גבי זה הכלל:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:4:1.english: And when it teaches "this is the general rule," it teaches it with regard to throwing - For [the Mishnah] was dealing just before it with one who throws to inflict a wound; and if an ordinary thrower is not exempted by remembering, how is it taught in connection with "this is the general rule"?

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:4:2.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - רישא מילי מילי קתני לה, ותרתי קתני: הזורק ונזכר, אי נמי לא נזכר וקלטה אחר כו'. והדר תני כללא לאתויי מעביר:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:4:2.english: Rather, Rava said - The first clause [of the mishna] teaches it [as] separate matters, and it teaches two [cases]: "One who throws and remembers," [or] "alternatively, he did not remember and another caught it," etc. And afterward it teaches a general rule to include one who carries.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:5:1.english: [The Mishnah] is incomplete, etc. - And in fact, it teaches one [case].

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:5:2.hebrew: שחזר ושכח - קודם שתנוח, דהוה ליה תחילתו וסופו שגגה. ואשמעינן נזכר דתנא בה לרבותא, דאע"ג דהואי ידיעה בינתיים מיחייב, דאין ידיעה לחצי שיעור, דהיינו כאין בידו להחזיר:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:5:2.english: Where one then forgot - Before it comes to rest, so that its beginning and its end are unwitting. And it teaches us [the case of] "and he remembered" that [the Mishnah] taught therein to show a novelty: that even though there was awareness in the interim, he is liable, because awareness has no [effect] for half a measure, which is like [a case where] it is not in his power to bring [it] back.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:6:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> שכל חייבי חטאות כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:6:1.english: This is the reading: that all who are liable [to bring] sin-offerings, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:6:2.hebrew: איתמר, ב' אמות בשוגג, ב' אמות במזיד, ב' אמות בשוגג, רבה אמר פטור, רבא אמר חייב - שתי אמות במזיד, שנזכר לאחר שתי אמות ראשונות, וחזר ושכח בב' האחרונות:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:6:2.english: It was stated: Two cubits unwittingly, two cubits intentionally, two cubits unwittingly — Rabbah says he is exempt; Rava says he is liable - "Two cubits intentionally" — [meaning] that he remembered after the first two cubits, and then forgot again during the last two [cubits].

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:7:1.hebrew: דר"ג - לקמן בפרק הבונה:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:7:1.english: Of Rabban Gamliel - Later, in the chapter [entitled] HaBoneh.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:7:2.hebrew: התם דכי גמר שיעורא בשוגג גמר - הכותב ב' אותיות בב' העלמות, דמחייב בה ר"ג, באות השניה נגמר השיעור, ואף הוא בשוגג. אבל הכא, בשתי אמצעיות שהן במזיד נגמר השיעור, כדמפרש ואזיל לה במעביר ושתי אמצעיות מזיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:7:2.english: There, when the measure was completed, it was completed unwittingly - One who writes two letters in two lapses of awareness, regarding which Rabban Gamliel holds him liable: with the second letter the measure is completed, and that too is unwittingly. However, here, with the two middle [cubits], which are [done] intentionally, the measure is completed, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain regarding one who carries [an object] and the two middle [cubits] are intentional.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:8:1.hebrew: שוגג הוא - שהרי אין בידו לעכבה, וכיון שחזר ושכח חייב, דלא נגמרה מלאכה עד שעת הנחה שהיא לסוף, ובשוגג:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:8:1.english: He is unwitting - For it is not in his power to stop it; and once he forgot again, he is liable, because the labor was not completed until the time of placing [it] down, which is at the end, and [was done] unwittingly.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:8:2.hebrew: אלא במעביר - וכיון דבידו לעמוד בסוף ב' אמות האמצעיות, אשתכח דגמר שיעורא במזיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:8:2.english: Rather, with one who carries - And since it is in his power to stop at the end of the two middle cubits, it turns out that he completed the measure intentionally.

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:9:1.hebrew: התם הוא דבידו - שלא לחזור ולכתוב השניה. הלכך, כי חזר ושכח, הויא לה שגגה אחריתי ולא גמרה לקמייתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:9:1.english: There, it is in his power - not to go back and write the second [letter]. Therefore, when he subsequently forgot, it is a separate unwitting transgression, and it does not complete the first [one].

Rashi on Shabbat 102a:9:2.hebrew: אבל הכא אין בידו - להחזיר כשנזכר, כדמפרש ואזיל בזורק. הלכך, כולה חדא שגגה היא, ומר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא ולא פליגי:
Rashi on Shabbat 102a:9:2.english: But here it is not in his control - to bring [it] back when he remembers, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain, [referring] to one who throws. Therefore, the entire [act] is one unwitting transgression, and one master stated one [case] and the other master stated another [case], and they do not disagree.

Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:10:1.hebrew: אמר רבא זרק בפי כלב - ל"ג "ונחה בפי כלב", ד"נחה" משמע מעצמה, כדא"ר יוחנן בפ"ק (לעיל שבת דף ה.): "זרק חפץ ונח לתוך ידו של חבירו חייב", ומסיק דקמ"ל אף על גב דלא אחשביה לידיה; והכא מסיק דקא מכוין, ומחשבתו משויא ליה מקום:
Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:10:1.english: Rava said: [If one] threw [it] into the mouth of a dog - We do not read "and it came to rest in the mouth of a dog," for "came to rest" [nachah] implies on its own, as Rabbi Yochanan said in the first chapter (above, Shabbat 5a): "If one threw an object and it came to rest in his fellow's hand, he is liable," and [the Gemara there] concludes that it teaches us [that he is liable] even though he did not designate his hand [as a place of rest]; whereas here [the Gemara] concludes that he intended [to throw it there], and his intention makes it a [significant] place:

Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:12:1.hebrew: רבי מאיר אומר אם היתה שבת והוציאו בפיו כו' - פי' בקונטרס דלהכי נקט אם היתה שבת, דמשום יוה"כ לא מיחייב, דאין עירוב והוצאה ליוה"כ. ולא הויא מסקנא הכי בפרק אמרו לו (כריתות דף יד.), דנדחו דברי רפרם שהיה מפרש כן; ומסיק דנקט שבת כדי להרבות בחטאות, ולחייבו אף משום שבת [ויוה"כ]:
Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:12:1.english: "Rabbi Meir says: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out in his mouth, etc." - Rashi explains that [the Mishnah] stated "if it was Shabbat" because one is not liable on account of Yom Kippur, as there is no eruv or [prohibition of] carrying out on Yom Kippur. However, this is not the conclusion in the chapter [entitled] Amru Lo (Keritot 14a), for the words of Rafram, who explained it this way, were rejected; rather, [the Gemara there] concludes that it stated "Shabbat" in order to multiply sin-offerings, and to make him liable on account of Shabbat [and Yom Kippur] as well.

Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:12:2.hebrew: והוציאו בפיו חייב - כולהו בהדי הדדי קא אתו, דבליעתו הויא הנחה אע"פ שמהלך, כדאמרינן (לעיל שבת דף פ.): "כתיבתן זו היא הנחתן". ואע"ג דפיו למעלה מי' ואינו רחב ד', בטל הוא אגב רה"ר. ולא דמי לבוכיאר ביריעה, דאמר בריש פרקין (לעיל שבת דף צו:) דבמקום פטור קא אזיל, דהתם מקום קביעות הוה טפי; ודמי לטרסקל, דאמר בפ"ק (דף ה.) דלמטה מי' הוי רה"ר, והכא אפילו למעלה מי' בטל אגב רשות הרבים. ועוד, דמעביר למעלה מי' כלמטה, וחשיב מונח ברשות הרבים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:12:2.english: And he carried it out in his mouth, he is liable - All of them [the acts of carrying out and swallowing] come together [simultaneously], for his swallowing is [considered] a placing down, even though he is walking, as we say (above, Shabbat 80a): "Their writing is their placing down." And even though his mouth is above ten [handbreadths] and is not four [handbreadths] wide, it is nullified to the public domain. And it is not comparable to a weaver's shuttle in the curtain, of which [the Gemara] says at the beginning of our chapter (above, Shabbat 96b) that it travels in an exempt area, for there it is more of a fixed place; and it is comparable to a basket, of which [the Gemara] says in the first chapter (5a) that below ten [handbreadths] it is [considered] a public domain, and here, even above ten [handbreadths] it is nullified to the public domain. And furthermore, one who carries [an object] above ten [handbreadths] is like [one who carries] below [ten handbreadths], and it is considered resting in the public domain.

Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:2:1.hebrew: סיפא אתאן ללכתא ומיתנא - אבל רישא מיירי בלא לכתא ומיתנא, וה"ה אפילו בלא נזכר פטור, כיון שקלטה כלב או נשרפה. והא דנקט נזכר — לאשמעינן דאפילו בנזכר דוקא קלטה כלב או נשרפה פטור משום דלא נחה, הא נחה — חייב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:2:1.english: [In] the latter clause, we have come to [a case of] a bolt and a cord - However, the first clause [of the Mishnah] deals with [a case] without a bolt and a cord, and the same applies even without [his] remembering — he is exempt, since a dog caught it or it was burned. And [the reason] that [the Mishnah] stated "remembered" is to teach us that even where he remembered, it is specifically [when] a dog caught it or it was burned [that] he is exempt, because it did not come to rest; [if] it came to rest, [however,] he is liable.

Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:3:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא במעביר - וההוא דחבורה איירי בלכתא ומיתנא, ואין ר"י יודע למה הוצרך להשמיענו ההיא דחבורה: מה לי חבורה, מה לי מעביר? וכן לרבא דקאמר "תרתי קתני", אמאי תנא ההיא דחבורה? כיון דתנא "הזורק ונזכר פטור", ה"נ בחבורה, דמ"ש:
Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:3:1.english: "Rather, Rava said: [It was stated] with regard to carrying" - And that [case] of [inflicting a] wound is speaking of a bolt and a cord. And the Ri does not know why it was necessary to teach us that [case] of [inflicting a] wound: what is the difference between [inflicting a] wound and carrying? And similarly, according to Rava, who says, "Two [separate matters] were taught," why did [the mishna] teach that [case] of [inflicting a] wound? Since it taught [that] one who throws and remembers is exempt, so too [is the law] with [inflicting a] wound, for what is the difference?

Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:5:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר חסורי מחסרא כו' - אין זה ממש חסורי מחסרא, דמשנה כמו שהיא שנויה יש לפרש כן, אלא כדי לפרשה קאמר בלשון חסורי מחסרא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:5:1.english: Rav Ashi said: "It is incomplete, etc." - This is not literally [a case of] "it is incomplete," for the Mishnah as it is taught can be explained this way; rather, in order to explain it, [Rav Ashi] says [it] using the phrasing "it is incomplete":

Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:8:1.hebrew: ובמאי אי בזורק שוגג הוא - אע"ג דכי גמר שיעוריה במזיד גמר, מ"מ כיון דבתחילת זריקה הוי שוגג ואין יכול להחזירה, ובהנחה נמי שוגג הוא — חשיב כאילו מתחלה ועד סוף הויא חדא שגגה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 102a:8:1.english: And in what [case]? If with regard to one who throws, he is unwitting - Even though when he completes his [requisite] measure he completes [it] intentionally, nevertheless, since at the beginning of the throw he was unwitting and cannot bring it back, and at the landing as well he is [considered] unwitting, it is considered as though from beginning to end it was one unwitting act.
